The design of transonic compressor cascades using the hodograph method is presented in this paper.
Previous research had focused on using the hodograph method for transonic turbine cascades, but not compressor cascades.
The key design requirements are: uniform and smooth flow in the nozzle, reasonable sonic line location, and desired aerodynamic characteristics in the subsonic region.
The analytical solution of the mixed-type hodograph equation is used in the supersonic regions, while the numerical solution of the Chaplygin equation is used in the subsonic regions.
Additional boundary conditions are used to improve the accuracy of the approximate compressible function in the subsonic regions.
The 'Shock wave-Meanstreamline Turn Method' is used to account for the flow turning caused by strong shock waves.
Two compressor cascade designs are presented: the J-3-Type and the Ma-Type.
The J-3-Type cascade has an outlet Mach number of 0.62, outlet flow angle of 45 degrees, and inlet Mach number of 1.22.
The velocity distribution of the J-3-Type cascade matches well with the Time Marching numerical method.
The Ma-Type cascade profile matches well with the cascade design provided in Reference 4.
The hodograph method can accurately model the supersonic and subsonic flow regions in transonic compressor cascades.
The 'Shock wave-Meanstreamline Turn Method' allows the hodograph method to account for the effects of strong shock waves.
The systematic design process using analytical and numerical solutions is a key advantage of the hodograph method.
Potential limitations include the accuracy of the approximate compressible function and the computational effort required.
The hodograph method provides a comprehensive approach to the design of transonic compressor cascades.
